newsitem.title: USA: Phillips Petroleum E&P oper net up 34 pct.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Petroleum E&P oper net up 34 pct.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co exploration and production net operating income rose 34 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to $202 million from $151 million as the company reported a rise in net operating income to $247 million from $210 million.
Net operating income per share rose to $0.94, slightly below analysts' expectations of $0.95, from $0.80, the company said on Wednesday.
Net income was $227 million, or $0.86 per share, down from $695 million, $2.65 per share, a year ago.
The year ago net includes a $565 million tax benefit.
The company said on Wednesday that higher crude oil and natural gas prices offset a four percent decline in production worldwide.
Refining and marketing operating net was $9 million against $7 million a year ago.
Refinery runs were 83 percent of capacity, down from 95 percent due to maintenance at the company's 200,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery at Sweeney, Texas.
Chemicals net operating income was $72 million versus $77 million a year. Gas processing net operating income was $28 million, the same as a year ago.

Phillips chief executive Wayne Allen said that the company would benefit from the start of gas injection facilities at the J-Block in the UK North Sea and increasing production at the Mahogany field in the Gulf of Mexico.

"Results should also be positively affected by the completion of the refinery turnaround and the restart of the idled ethylene unit at the Sweeney facility; the paraxylene expnasion at the Puerto Rico Core facility; and the expansion of a high-density polyethylene facility in Singapore.
